correctness.rationale: Substitution of the published density into the Rényi definition gives an exact Gaussian-weighted integral. Rewriting that integral as an expectation under a centered normal law with variance \(1/\gamma\) is algebraic. Polynomial growth of \(q(x)^\gamma\) and at-most-exponential growth of \(\cosh(\lambda x)^\gamma\) are dominated by the Gaussian factor for every real \(\gamma>0\), proving existence. The source's finite multinomial and binomial expansions require integer exponent; noninteger powers require an infinite generalized expansion or direct integration. A standalone checker independently matches direct quadrature, the expectation representation, and the normal benchmark.

The source explicitly states the theorem for all positive real orders other than one and then uses finite sums indexed through the order. Five focused published-finding corpus searches and targeted public searches for the DOI, NTPN, Rényi, noninteger order, multinomial, and correction aliases found no model-specific correction. value.rationale: Rényi entropy is a named theorem and one of the paper's advertised analytical properties. Its order is intrinsically a real parameter, so restricting a purported all-order formula to integers is not cosmetic. The correction preserves entropy existence, supplies an exact and numerically stable representation for all admissible real orders, gives a decisive standard-normal benchmark, and carefully leaves the source's integer-order contour intact.
